pages.title: Overview
pages.lead: Mark edges on a mesh. Get stitches, lines and checks along them, baked to UV masks.

sections.heading: What it does
sections.body:
Pick edges in Blender, and the add-on draws patterns along them. Each pattern bakes to a 16-bit mask PNG.

Use the masks in painting apps such as Substance 3D Painter or Clip Studio Paint.

sections.heading: Three kinds of layers
sections.body:
- **Stitches**: dashed or zigzag, a set distance in from the edge.
- **Line Art**: solid lines of one real width.
- **Grid**: a checkerboard laid from a marked edge.

sections.heading: Why on the 3D surface
sections.body:
Sizes are real millimetres on the model, so stretched UVs don't change them.

Lines keep their distance along the cloth and stay sharp at marked corners.

sections.heading: Requirements
sections.body: Blender 4.2 or newer, and a mesh with UVs.

pages.title: Install and first mask
pages.lead: Install, then bake a stitch mask along a hem.

sections.heading: Install
sections.body:
- From Blender: Edit › Preferences › Get Extensions, search *Pattern Masks*.
- From a zip: Get Extensions › ▾ › **Install from Disk…**
keys: Press N in the 3D View to open the sidebar, then click this tab.
The layer list on top, then marking edges and corners, the selected layer's settings, and the bake.

sections.heading: Add a stitch layer
sections.body: Each pattern is a layer in the list: one **Stitches** layer per object, and as many **Line Art** and **Grid** layers as you like.

sections.heading: Give it the hem
sections.body: A layer draws only along its own edges. In Blender, pick them in Edit Mode first.

sections.heading: Set the stitches
sections.body: Sizes are real millimetres on the model, whatever its size.
keys: How far the stitches sit from the edge.

sections.heading: Bake
sections.body: Save the .blend, then press the bake button at the bottom of the panel. Each layer gives one 16-bit PNG per material, in the `stitch_masks` folder next to the .blend.

sections.heading: Paint with it
sections.body:
In Substance 3D Painter, import the PNG and use it as a grayscale mask on a fill layer.

> Other apps and file names: [Bake and use](bake.html).

sections.heading: What it changes
sections.body: Only edge and vertex attributes. Shape, UVs and materials stay as they are.

pages.title: Layers and edges
pages.lead: Every layer draws along its own edges. Try each idea below on the skirt piece.

sections.heading: The layer list
sections.body: Each pattern is a row in the list.
keys: Also used as the file name.
Shows the layer. A hidden layer isn't baked.
In the panel header: hides or shows every layer's marked edges and corners at once. Each layer keeps its own toggle.
In the panel header: turns live updates on and off.
Shows while live updates are off: rebuilds once.
**Clear All Layers**: removes every object's layers, marked edges and previews from the scene.

sections.heading: Edges row
sections.body:
Select edges in Edit Mode, pick the layer in the list, then use the **Edges** row.

> Each layer keeps its own edges.
keys: Adds the selected edges to the layer.
Takes them out of the layer.
Selects all of the layer's edges.
Follows another layer's edges: see [Reference](#reference). It shows pressed while the layer follows one.

sections.heading: Reference
sections.body:
A layer can use the edges of another one, and follows when those change.

> To leave a few of them out, select them and press **−**: they turn red here, and the other layer keeps them.

In the link menu the layer being followed is ticked; **Clear Reference** stops following it.

sections.heading: Sharp corners
sections.body:
Where two edges meet at a tip, a line rounds the corner. To keep it sharp, mark the vertex on the **Sharp Corners** row.

> The marks are shared by all layers.
keys: Shows the marked corners in the view.

sections.heading: Flip Side
sections.body:
**Flip Side** moves every line to the other side of its edges.

Use it for edges inside the mesh. A border has no cloth on its other side, so its lines disappear.

> Shared by all layers.

pages.title: Stitches
pages.lead: Dashed or zigzag stitches, a set distance in from the edge.

sections.heading: Dashed and zigzag
sections.body: Two styles: **Dashed**, separate stitches, and **Zigzag**, one thread going back and forth.

sections.heading: Settings
keys: Distance from the edge, measured along the cloth.
Evens out the kinks a low-poly edge puts in the line. Mark the corners that should stay sharp.
**Dashed** draws separate stitches; **Zigzag** one thread going back and forth.
Stitch width; for a zigzag, the thread width.
Stitch length; for a zigzag, peak to peak.
How round the stitch ends are (100% is fully round).
How far a zigzag swings. Raise **Offset Inward** with it.

pages.title: Line art
pages.lead: Solid lines of one real width, from an outline to a band.

sections.heading: What it draws
sections.body: A solid line along the layer's edges: the same width everywhere on the model, following the edge's exact shape, sharp at marked corners. Add as many Line Art layers as you need.

sections.heading: Settings
keys: Distance from the edge to the line's outer side (0 = an outline).
Smooths the inner side between corners.
Line width, the same everywhere on the model.

pages.title: Grid
pages.lead: A checkerboard laid from a marked edge.

sections.heading: What it makes
sections.body:
Squares of one real size on the model, laid from a marked edge.

> Each grid bakes two masks: `_black.png` and `_white.png`.

sections.heading: Which edge to mark
sections.body: Mark one edge per piece, such as the waist. Every UV island with a marked edge gets filled.

sections.heading: Settings
keys: Slides the squares away from the edge.
Bows the lines slightly at random (0 = straight).
**Follow Loops** or **Unrolled**: see the two renders above.

pages.title: Presets
pages.lead: Save a layer's settings and reuse them in any file.

sections.heading: Save, apply and set a default
sections.body: > Ctrl+Z undoes applying a preset.
keys: Applies the starred preset, or the add-on's own values when none is starred.
Saves the current settings under that name.
Makes the preset the default for new layers of that kind.

pages.title: Bake and use
pages.lead: One PNG per layer and material.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
One PNG per layer and material, named from the object, the material and the layer.

- With several objects selected, one press bakes them all, each with its own settings.
- Fold the **Bake** section and its button stays in the title row.

> The bake runs in the background, so you can keep working.

sections.heading: Using the masks
sections.body:
- Substance 3D Painter: import the PNG and use it as a mask on a fill layer. Re-import it after each new bake.
- Clip Studio Paint: set **Background** to **White**, bake, open the PNG and use **Edit › Convert brightness to opacity**: the white turns clear and the marks stay. (It can't open a transparent PNG that holds very little.)
- Photoshop and other 2D apps: **Transparent** puts the mask in the alpha channel.

keys: Which UV map to bake into.

pages.title: Notes and limits
pages.lead: Good to know before you bake.

sections.heading: Mesh
sections.body:
- Modifiers are ignored. Apply them on a copy first.
- Lines skip notches narrower than twice their distance from the edge.
- Where cloth folds over itself, stitches bake only on the layer they belong to.

sections.heading: Grid
sections.body:
- **Follow Loops** forks where the piece widens. Larger squares mean fewer forks.
- **Unrolled** takes a second or two to compute, in the background.

sections.heading: Bake
sections.body:
- An 8192 bake needs about 2 GB of free memory.
- A face that crosses a UDIM tile border is baked into one tile only.

sections.heading: Questions
sections.body:
### Bake is greyed out
Show a layer and give it edges.

### Stitches are on the wrong side
Turn on **Flip Side**.

### A corner is cut off
Mark it on the **Sharp Corners** row.

### Painter shows the old mask
Re-import the file.
